C-PERFORMANCE-DOMAIN-REFACTOR.Summary: Reorganize domain as session/exercise/{set,performance}; rename workout exercise memberships to performances across code, schema, backups and documentation without changing workout behavior.

Goals.Goal: Move session to internal/domain/session, catalog exercise to internal/domain/session/exercise, and set/performance beneath that exercise package.
Replace SessionExercise/sessionexercise/session_exercises names with Performance/performance/performances, including operations, repositories, foreign keys and TUI ownership names.

Constraints.Constraint: Preserve UUID relationships, automatic positive session indices, unique(session_id, exercise_id), idempotent add, insertion ordering, cascade boundaries and referenced-catalog deletion protection.
Retain the existing CLI-generated single initial migration pair, editing its latest schema in place. Do not open or modify the real user database; no legacy database conversion is requested.
Use backup version 4 with performances and performance_id fields. Reject earlier versions before writes; retain atomic import and local credentials.
Retain records layout, catalog picker, body-weight percentage columns, help content and compact shared spacing; label the workout performance panel Performances <2>.
Preserve staged and unstaged user changes and the git index. Use constructors, existing source formatting and one operation per use-case file. Do not add committed automated tests.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No new workout features, relationship/cardinality changes, database reset, legacy data/backup conversion, or unrelated cleanup.
Do not rewrite archived change history; rename current durable graph/verification identifiers and file-local anchors only.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Only domain/session/exercise/{set,performance} remains for moved models; all imports compile without aliases for old packages.
Performance, PerformanceRepository, AddPerformance, DeletePerformance and ListPerformances replace their old names; sets reference PerformanceID and FindAllByPerformanceID.
The schema uses performances, performance_id and matching index names. Up/down/up yields seven tables and preserves constraints.
Version-4 JSON round trips workouts, catalog exercises, performances and sets; older versions and orphan/duplicate performances are rejected before mutation.
TUI selection, catalog creation/edit/add/removal, cascading set behavior, backup/restore and compact layouts remain correct with performance naming.

Current graph, verification commands, semantic anchors and README match the new names. Build/vet/format and temporary database/TUI scenarios pass. Apply/archive after successful checks, using the user’s continuing archive instruction.

Assumptions.Assumption: The explicit rename request authorizes the described mechanical refactor and public/internal symbol updates. Prior sequential execution and final archive preferences persist.
Performances remain one catalog exercise in one session; this naming change does not move sets under a performance subdirectory. The requested set and performance folders are siblings.
